I tried using Monday.com for a building project I had and the interface become totally unusably slow... no idea if this is fixed but it seems like an issue for a billion dollar company.
Monday is just plain bad, it's slow, it's not really useful. Looks like a bunch of solutions looking for problems put together in a frenzy.

Moving from Trello to monday.com was the biggest reason why we couldn't deliver in time an iOS project for a client... When 90% of the team decides to update tickets once a week instead of daily, simply because they HATE the tool, then you know you're in for an unpleasant ride. We're back on Trello now.

I use it at my current company. I don't like it. I don't like Jira either, but Jira is still far superior... Linking tickets to one another in Monday is really bad, data gets lost all the time, it's not good for retaining a record of work.
I worked at a company where Monday was the main interface between the back-office and the B2B clients we serviced. That was about as bad as you can expect.

This is one of the worst tools I've ever used and we tried hard for a year. Besides the interface being clunky and slow it lets you delete important things on accident with multiple people in our group having fallen victim to it's non intuitive UI.
We'd tried it for a little bit for a small 5-6 person team. It was slow as hell. Stopped using it.

Until a while ago, when a user landed on their board, we threw all the board data right into the client... it started to struggle and finally, crashed after a few thousand items. If we really pushed it, we could handle up to 20k items. Beyond that, it was game over.

Hmm maybe I missed something but isn't Monday some kind of do-all task management system? A client of mine forced us on it and the un-opinionated style made it quite crappy. You can basically have to do whatever all managers came up with randomly and it sucked.

I used monday.com a few years ago. Back then it was called 'dapulse'... I felt silly every time I said it. I just remember really wanting to like it because of how clean it was, but not really being able to. I think it required too much setup and customization for my liking.
I used it a few times, it's as good as the others. I don't think there ever will be a silver bullet, what works for some companies won't work for others. The real issues are people issues.
